passages.text: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem forty years. His mother’s name was Zibiah; she was from Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Joash became king when he was seven years old.
Joash ruled in Jerusalem.
Joash reigned for forty years.
Joash’s mother was Zibiah.
Zibiah came from Beersheba.
passages.original: בֶּן־ שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ יֹאָ֣שׁ בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ צִבְיָ֖ה מִבְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

passages.text: And Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
passages.sermon:
Joash was king of Judah.
Joash did what was right.
The LORD saw Joash’s actions as good.
Joash acted rightly while Jehoiada was priest.
Joash continued to do right as long as Jehoiada lived.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יוֹאָ֛שׁ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כָּל־ יְמֵ֖י יְהוֹיָדָ֥ע הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: Jehoiada took for himself two wives, and he had sons and daughters.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiada was a priest in Jerusalem.
Jehoiada took two wives.
Jehoiada had sons.
Jehoiada had daughters.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂא־ ל֥וֹ יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע נָשִׁ֣ים שְׁתָּ֑יִם וַיּ֖וֹלֶד בָּנִ֥ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Some time later, Joash set his heart on repairing the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Joash was king of Judah.
Joash lived during the time of Jehoiada the priest.
Some time passed.
Joash decided to repair the house of the LORD.
Joash set his heart on this work.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י אַחֲרֵיכֵ֑ן הָיָה֙ עִם־ לֵ֣ב יוֹאָ֔שׁ לְחַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So he gathered the priests and Levites and said, “Go out to the cities of Judah and collect the money due annually from all Israel, to repair the house of your God. Do it quickly.” The Levites, however, did not make haste.
passages.sermon:
Joash was the king of Judah.
Joash wanted to repair the house of the LORD.
Joash gathered the priests and the Levites.
Joash spoke to them.
He said, “Go out to the cities of Judah.
Collect money from all Israel.
Collect this money every year.
Use the money to repair the house of your God.
Do this quickly.”
The Levites did not act quickly.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבֹּץ֮ אֶת־ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֡ם צְא֣וּ לְעָרֵ֪י יְהוּדָ֟ה וְקִבְצוּ֩ מִכָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל כֶּ֜סֶף לְחַזֵּ֣ק׀ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם מִדֵּ֤י שָׁנָה֙ בְּשָׁנָ֔ה וְאַתֶּ֖ם תְּמַהֲר֣וּ לַדָּבָ֑ר וְלֹ֥א מִֽהֲר֖וּ הַֽלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: So the king called Jehoiada the high priest and said, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring from Judah and Jerusalem the tax imposed by Moses the servant of the LORD and by the assembly of Israel for the Tent of the Testimony?”
passages.sermon:
King Joash ruled over Judah.
Joash wanted to repair the house of the LORD.
Jehoiada served as the high priest.
Joash called Jehoiada to him.
Joash spoke to Jehoiada.
Joash asked Jehoiada a question.
Joash said, “Why have you not required the Levites to do their duty?”
Joash said, “The Levites must bring the tax from Judah and Jerusalem.”
Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded this tax for Israel.
The assembly of Israel also agreed to this tax.
The tax was for the Tent of the Testimony.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ לִֽיהוֹיָדָ֣ע הָרֹאשׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ מַדּ֙וּעַ֙ לֹֽא־ דָרַ֣שְׁתָּ עַל־ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְהָבִ֞יא מִֽיהוּדָ֣ה וּמִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶת־ מַשְׂאַת֙ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־ יְהוָ֔ה וְהַקָּהָ֖ל לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֽוּת׃

passages.text: For the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had even used the sacred objects of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
passages.sermon:
Athaliah was a wicked woman.
Her sons broke into the house of God.
They took the sacred objects from the house of the LORD.
They used these holy things for the worship of Baal.
passages.original: כִּ֤י עֲתַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ הַמִּרְשַׁ֔עַת בָּנֶ֥יהָ פָרְצ֖וּ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְגַם֙ כָּל־ קָדְשֵׁ֣י בֵית־ יְהוָ֔ה עָשׂ֖וּ לַבְּעָלִֽים׃

passages.text: At the king’s command a chest was made and placed outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The king gave a command.
The people made a chest.
They placed the chest outside.
They put it at the gate of the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ אֲר֣וֹן אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּתְּנֻ֛הוּ בְּשַׁ֥עַר בֵּית־ יְהוָ֖ה חֽוּצָה׃

passages.text: And a proclamation was issued in Judah and Jerusalem that they were to bring to the LORD the tax imposed by Moses the servant of God on Israel in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Judah and Jerusalem received a proclamation.
The leaders made an announcement.
They told the people to bring an offering to the LORD.
This offering was a tax.
Moses, the servant of God, had commanded this tax.
Moses gave this command to Israel in the wilderness.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנוּ־ ק֞וֹל בִּֽיהוּדָ֣ה וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם לְהָבִ֤יא לַֽיהוָה֙ מַשְׂאַ֞ת מֹשֶׁ֧ה עֶֽבֶד־ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: All the officers and all the people rejoiced and brought their contributions, and they dropped them in the chest until it was full.
passages.sermon:
The officers and the people felt joy.
They brought their contributions.
They put their gifts into the chest.
They continued until the chest was full.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כָל־ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְכָל־ הָעָ֑ם וַיָּבִ֛יאוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥יכוּ לָאָר֖וֹן עַד־ לְכַלֵּֽה׃

passages.text: Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king’s overseers and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the royal scribe and the officer of the high priest would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. They did this daily and gathered the money in abundance.
passages.sermon:
The Levites brought the chest to the king’s overseers.
The overseers checked the chest.
They saw there was a large amount of money.
The royal scribe came.
The officer of the high priest came.
They emptied the chest.
They carried the chest back to its place.
They did this every day.
They collected a great amount of money.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י בְּעֵת֩ יָבִ֨יא אֶת־ הָֽאָר֜וֹן אֶל־ פְּקֻדַּ֣ת הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ בְּיַ֣ד הַלְוִיִּם֒ וְכִרְאוֹתָ֞ם כִּי־ רַ֣ב הַכֶּ֗סֶף וּבָ֨א סוֹפֵ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וּפְקִיד֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וִיעָ֙רוּ֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אָר֔וֹן וְיִשָּׂאֻ֖הוּ וִֽישִׁיבֻ֣הוּ אֶל־ מְקֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֤ה עָשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם׀ בְּי֔וֹם וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ־ כֶ֖סֶף לָרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Then the king and Jehoiada would give the money to those who supervised the labor on the house of the LORD to hire stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, as well as workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The king and Jehoiada took the money.
They gave the money to the supervisors of the work on the house of the LORD.
The supervisors hired stonecutters.
The supervisors hired carpenters.
The stonecutters and carpenters worked to restore the house of the LORD.
The supervisors also hired workers in iron.
The supervisors hired workers in bronze.
The workers in iron and bronze repaired the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וִֽיהוֹיָדָ֗ע אֶל־ עוֹשֵׂה֙ מְלֶ֙אכֶת֙ עֲבוֹדַ֣ת בֵּית־ יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּֽהְי֤וּ שֹׂכְרִים֙ חֹצְבִ֣ים וְחָרָשִׁ֔ים לְחַדֵּ֖שׁ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠גַם לְחָרָשֵׁ֤י בַרְזֶל֙ וּנְחֹ֔שֶׁת לְחַזֵּ֖ק אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So the workmen labored, and in their hands the repair work progressed. They restored the house of God according to its specifications, and they reinforced it.
passages.sermon:
The workmen labored.
The repair work progressed in their hands.
They restored the house of God.
They followed its specifications.
They reinforced the house of God.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ עֹשֵׂ֣י הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה וַתַּ֧עַל אֲרוּכָ֛ה לַמְּלָאכָ֖ה בְּיָדָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲמִ֜ידוּ אֶת־ בֵּ֧ית הָֽאֱלֹהִ֛ים עַל־ מַתְכֻּנְתּ֖וֹ וַֽיְאַמְּצֻֽהוּ׃

passages.text: When they were finished, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada to make with it the articles for the house of the LORD—utensils for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and other objects of gold and silver. Throughout the days of Jehoiada, burnt offerings were presented regularly in the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The workers finished their task.
They brought the remaining money to the king and to Jehoiada.
The king and Jehoiada used the money to make items for the house of the LORD.
They made utensils for serving in the temple.
They made utensils for burnt offerings.
They made dishes.
They made other objects of gold and silver.
People offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD regularly.
They did this throughout the days of Jehoiada.
passages.original: וּֽכְכַלּוֹתָ֡ם הֵבִ֣יאוּ לִפְנֵי֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וִֽיהוֹיָדָ֜ע אֶת־ שְׁאָ֣ר הַכֶּ֗סֶף וַיַּעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ כֵלִ֤ים לְבֵית־ יְהוָה֙ כְּלֵ֣י שָׁרֵ֔ת וְהַעֲל֣וֹת וְכַפּ֔וֹת וּכְלֵ֥י זָהָ֖ב וָכָ֑סֶף וַ֠יִּֽהְיוּ מַעֲלִ֨ים עֹל֤וֹת בְּבֵית־ יְהוָה֙ תָּמִ֔יד כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י יְהוֹיָדָֽע׃פ

passages.text: When Jehoiada was old and full of years, he died at the age of 130.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiada was a priest in Israel.
Jehoiada lived a long life.
Jehoiada became very old.
Jehoiada reached the age of 130 years.
Jehoiada died when he was 130 years old.
passages.original: וַיִּזְקַ֧ן יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע וַיִּשְׂבַּ֥ע יָמִ֖ים וַיָּמֹ֑ת בֶּן־ מֵאָ֧ה וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה בְּמוֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Jehoiada was buried with the kings in the City of David, because he had done what was good in Israel for God and His temple.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiada was a priest in Israel.
Jehoiada did good things for Israel.
Jehoiada served God faithfully.
Jehoiada cared for God’s temple.
The people buried Jehoiada in the City of David.
They buried him with the kings.
They did this because Jehoiada had done what was good for Israel, for God, and for God’s house.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְעִיר־ דָּוִ֖יד עִם־ הַמְּלָכִ֑ים כִּֽי־ עָשָׂ֤ה טוֹבָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעִ֥ם הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּבֵיתֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: After the death of Jehoiada, however, the officials of Judah came and paid homage to the king, and he listened to them.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiada was a priest in Judah.
Jehoiada died.
After Jehoiada died, the officials of Judah came to the king.
The officials of Judah bowed down before the king.
The king listened to the officials of Judah.
passages.original: וְאַֽחֲרֵ֥י מוֹת֙ יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע בָּ֚אוּ שָׂרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֖וּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אָ֛ז שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and idols. So wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah and Jerusalem turned away from God.
They left the house of the LORD.
The LORD is the God of their fathers.
They served Asherah poles.
They served idols.
God became angry with Judah and Jerusalem.
God’s anger came because of their guilt.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַזְב֗וּ אֶת־ בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּֽעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־ הָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הָֽעֲצַבִּ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־ קֶ֗צֶף עַל־ יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּאַשְׁמָתָ֖ם זֹֽאת׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the LORD sent prophets to bring the people back to Him and to testify against them; but they would not listen.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sent prophets to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD wanted the people to return to Him.
The prophets warned the people.
The people did not listen to the prophets.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח בָּהֶם֙ נְבִאִ֔ים לַהֲשִׁיבָ֖ם אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּעִ֥ידוּ בָ֖ם וְלֹ֥א הֶאֱזִֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood up before the people and said to them, “This is what God says: ‘Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was the son of Jehoiada the priest.
The Spirit of God came upon Zechariah.
Zechariah stood before the people.
Zechariah spoke to the people.
Zechariah said, “This is what God says.”
God asked, “Why do you break the commandments of the LORD?”
God said, “You cannot succeed because you have left the LORD.”
God said, “Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.”
passages.original: וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֗ים לָֽבְשָׁה֙ אֶת־ זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד מֵעַ֣ל לָעָ֑ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָהֶ֜ם כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים לָמָה֩ אַתֶּ֨ם עֹבְרִ֜ים אֶת־ מִצְוֺ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְלֹ֣א תַצְלִ֔יחוּ כִּֽי־ עֲזַבְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיַּֽעֲזֹ֥ב אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But they conspired against Zechariah, and by order of the king, they stoned him in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people made a secret plan against Zechariah.
The king gave an order to kill Zechariah.
The people threw stones at Zechariah.
They killed Zechariah with stones.
They did this in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּקְשְׁר֣וּ עָלָ֔יו וַיִּרְגְּמֻ֥הוּ אֶ֖בֶן בְּמִצְוַ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בַּחֲצַ֖ר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Thus King Joash failed to remember the kindness that Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had extended to him. Instead, Joash killed Jehoiada’s son. As he lay dying, Zechariah said, “May the LORD see this and call you to account.”
passages.sermon:
King Joash ruled over Judah.
Jehoiada was a priest.
Jehoiada had shown great kindness to Joash.
Joash did not remember this kindness.
Joash killed Jehoiada’s son, Zechariah.
Zechariah was dying.
As Zechariah died, he spoke.
Zechariah said, “May the LORD see this.”
Zechariah said, “May the LORD call you to account.”
passages.original: וְלֹא־ זָכַ֞ר יוֹאָ֣שׁ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הַחֶ֙סֶד֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה יְהוֹיָדָ֤ע אָבִיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־ בְּנ֑וֹ וּכְמוֹת֣וֹ אָמַ֔ר יֵ֥רֶא יְהוָ֖ה וְיִדְרֹֽשׁ׃פ

passages.text: In the spring, the army of Aram went to war against Joash. They entered Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people, and they sent all the plunder to their king in Damascus.
passages.sermon:
The army of Aram attacked King Joash in the spring.
They entered Judah.
They entered Jerusalem.
They destroyed all the leaders of the people.
They took all the plunder.
They sent the plunder to their king in Damascus.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ לִתְקוּפַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה עָלָיו֮ חֵ֣יל אֲרָם֒ וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ אֶל־ יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּשְׁחִ֛יתוּ אֶת־ כָּל־ שָׂרֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם מֵעָ֑ם וְכָל־ שְׁלָלָ֥ם שִׁלְּח֖וּ לְמֶ֥לֶךְ דַּרְמָֽשֶׂק׃

passages.text: Although the Aramean army had come with only a few men, the LORD delivered into their hand a very great army. Because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, judgment was executed on Joash.
passages.sermon:
The Aramean army came with only a few men.
The LORD gave a very large army into the hand of the Arameans.
Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers.
Because of this, the LORD allowed judgment against Joash.
passages.original: כִּי֩ בְמִצְעַ֨ר אֲנָשִׁ֜ים בָּ֣אוּ׀ חֵ֣יל אֲרָ֗ם וַֽיהוָה֙ נָתַ֨ן בְּיָדָ֥ם חַ֙יִל֙ לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עָֽזְב֔וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶת־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ עָשׂ֥וּ שְׁפָטִֽים׃

passages.text: And when the Arameans had withdrawn, they left Joash severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for shedding the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died and was buried in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
passages.sermon:
Joash was king of Judah.
The Arameans attacked Judah and Jerusalem.
They left Joash with many wounds.
Joash’s own servants turned against him.
They conspired because Joash killed the son of Jehoiada the priest.
The servants killed Joash while he lay on his bed.
Joash died.
People buried Joash in the City of David.
They did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
passages.original: וּבְלֶכְתָּ֣ם מִמֶּ֗נּוּ כִּֽי־ עָזְב֣וּ אֹתוֹ֮ בְּמַחֲלִיִּים רַבִּים֒ הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו עֲבָדָ֗יו בִּדְמֵי֙ בְּנֵי֙ יְהוֹיָדָ֣ע הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וַיַּֽהַרְגֻ֥הוּ עַל־ מִטָּת֖וֹ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֙הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֥א קְבָרֻ֖הוּ בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Those who conspired against Joash were Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
passages.sermon:
Joash was king of Judah.
Two men conspired against Joash.
The first man was Zabad.
Zabad was the son of Shimeath.
Shimeath was an Ammonitess.
The second man was Jehozabad.
Jehozabad was the son of Shimrith.
Shimrith was a Moabitess.
passages.original: וְאֵ֖לֶּה הַמִּתְקַשְּׁרִ֣ים עָלָ֑יו זָבָ֗ד בֶּן־ שִׁמְעָת֙ הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֔ית וִיה֣וֹזָבָ֔ד בֶּן־ שִׁמְרִ֖ית הַמּוֹאָבִֽית׃

passages.text: The accounts of the sons of Joash, as well as the many pronouncements about him and about the restoration of the house of God, are indeed written in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
The Book of the Kings contains a record.
This record includes the sons of Joash.
It also includes many pronouncements about Joash.
It describes the restoration of the house of God.
Amaziah was the son of Joash.
Amaziah became king after Joash.
passages.original: וּבָנָ֞יו וְרֹב הַמַּשָּׂ֣א עָלָ֗יו וִיסוֹד֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־ מִדְרַ֖שׁ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֑ים וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
